description: Archives a NINJAM jam to disk as each player's raw OGG intervals with an index beside them, and exports the result as a session file for Ableton

params.text: Arms the archive, so every interval the room sends is written to disk from the moment it is switched on
Includes your own transmitted mix in the archive alongside the other players'

notes: It records nothing unless it is placed immediately beside a Ninjam module; on its own it can only export a jam folder recorded earlier
Recordings go into a dated folder under the jams folder, with a JSON lines index placing every interval on the session timeline
The audio is stored as the bytes that came off the wire, with no re-encoding
Nothing is written unless this module is armed next to a joined Ninjam module
menu: Export Ableton Live set (.als)… — prompts for a jam folder and writes a session file from its recordings: the Looper grid as clips, each player on an arrangement lane, tempo and bars matching
Export .als when recording stops — when on, the session file is built automatically as soon as recording ends
Target Live edition: Standard / Suite (full), Lite (8 tracks: 6 loops + players + TX) — chooses a track per player, or a fold-down to eight tracks with every player merged onto one lane
Choose folder… — picks the folder the jam recordings are written to
Reset to ~/Music/jams — puts the jams folder back to the default
Open jams folder — opens the jams folder in the file browser
